confidence._comment: MIG-022 §E.1 (PJ-042) — labels for the Confidence enum that catalogers self-report on each ReasoningTrail. Shown in [brackets] next to the cataloger name in the per-cataloger trail rows. Raw enum strings (high/medium/low/abstain) were previously rendered untranslated; confidenceLabel() in SourceReviewPanel now wraps with $t() fallback to the raw enum on missing key.

reasoning._comment: MIG-022 §E.2 (PJ-041) — i18n templates for per-cataloger reasoning prose. Each cataloger emits {key, params} alongside the raw English `reasoning` field. Frontend renders $t('cece.reasoning.<key>', params) when the template field is present; falls back to raw `reasoning` for legacy composite_json blobs and the Reasoning cataloger (whose prose comes from the LLM). Placeholders use {paramName} syntax. Numeric weights are pre-formatted as 2-decimal strings in Rust to avoid locale-specific number formatting.

description.perception: First-hand sensory observation. What you saw, heard, touched, measured yourself in the present moment.

description.comparison: Knowledge by analogy to a known thing. Legal qiyas, scientific reasoning by analogy, structural parallels.
description.postulation: Inference to the best explanation. Positing an unobserved fact required to explain an observed one (arthapatti).
description.non-apprehension: Knowledge of absence. Something is NOT there because perception of it fails (anupalabdhi).
description.memory: Recall of past experience. What you remember from earlier observations, conversations, or learnings.
description.innate-disposition: Pre-experiential knowing — basic moral or logical truths every healthy mind recognizes (fitrah / nous).

description.revelation: Sacred-text or prophetic transmission — Qur'an, scripture, divine command (al-wahy).

inspector360.title: 360.3D
inspector360.noData: Open a note to see its 360° view
inspector360.help_axis_stratum: Vertical axis — stratum. The 8 rows from L1 Datum at the bottom to L8 Worldview at the top represent intellectual altitude. The active note's row is highlighted in purple. Dots above your row are connections at higher altitudes (more abstract); dots below are at lower altitudes (more concrete).
inspector360.help_axis_type: Horizontal axis — link type. The 8 columns are the 7 typed link directions plus Untyped. Each connected note becomes a coloured dot in the cell where its stratum meets the typed direction it shares with the active note. Diagonal stripes mean the cell is empty — a blind spot at that (stratum, type) intersection.
inspector360.help_stratum_8: Worldview — the deepest layer of your thinking. Foundational beliefs and paradigm-spanning principles. The lens through which all other thinking is filtered. A note here is something you would defend at the level of identity.
inspector360.help_stratum_7: Paradigm — an established framework of thinking. A coherent system of principles that organizes how you approach a domain (your model of physics, your theory of leadership, your practice of Islam). One step below Worldview.
inspector360.help_stratum_6: Theory — a structured explanation that connects multiple principles into a model. A theory both predicts and explains; a principle on its own does not.
inspector360.help_stratum_5: Principle — a general law or rule abstracted from concepts. "Power corrupts." "Compounding rewards patience." Principles are reusable across domains.
inspector360.help_stratum_4: Concept — an abstract idea or category. Concepts name a pattern across many specific instances. A note at L4 has been refined enough to stand on its own as a defined idea.
inspector360.help_stratum_3: Proposition — a specific claim or assertion. Stronger than information (it has a stance), weaker than a principle (it is not yet generalized).
inspector360.help_stratum_2: Information — processed data with meaning. Information is what data becomes after you have made sense of it, but before you have drawn a claim from it.
inspector360.help_stratum_1: Datum — a single fact, observation, or quote. The atomic unit of knowledge. A date, a number, a passage transcribed verbatim.
inspector360.help_type_supports: Supports — this note backs up another note's claim. Annotated as [[target|supports]]. Use when the target's argument is strengthened by what this note contains.
inspector360.help_type_contradicts: Contradicts — this note disputes or challenges another note's claim. [[target|contradicts]]. Tracking contradictions is intellectual honesty: every Supports without a Contradicts is one-sided thinking.
inspector360.help_type_causes: Causes — this note describes a causal relationship. A leads to B. [[target|causes]]. Use when there is a directional cause-and-effect, not just correlation.
inspector360.help_type_derives_from: Derives From — this note's reasoning is based on another note. The target is the source. [[target|derives-from]]. The trust depth (e.g. d11) in the dimension strip counts how deep this chain runs to reach a root.
inspector360.help_type_generalizes: Generalizes — this note draws a broader pattern from specific examples. [[target|generalizes]]. Use when this note abstracts upward from the target.
inspector360.help_type_exemplifies: Exemplifies — this note is an instance or example of a broader idea in the target. [[target|exemplifies]]. The opposite direction of Generalizes.
inspector360.help_type_part_of: Part Of — this note is a component of a larger idea, system, or hierarchy in the target. [[target|part-of]]. Structural composition rather than logical relationship.
inspector360.help_type_untyped: Untyped — plain wikilinks without a relationship type, written as [[target]]. The link exists but you have not yet committed to what it means. Untyped is a starting state; mature thinking moves links toward typed forms over time.
inspector360.help_dim_stratum: Stratum — the note's intellectual altitude on the 8-level hierarchy from L1 Datum to L8 Worldview. Computed from word count, inbound links, source depth, and the typed-link directions you have used. The matrix highlights this row in purple.
inspector360.help_dim_maturity: Maturity — the note's lifecycle state: Seed → Sapling → Evergreen → Canonical → Wilting. Tracks whether the note is raw, growing, established, locked, or decaying.
inspector360.help_dim_origin: Origin — where the note came from: Received (read from a source), Discovered (your own thinking), or Mixed. The depth number (e.g. d11) is how far the source chain runs through derives-from links to reach a root.
inspector360.help_dim_stage: Stage — how formally the idea is committed: Fleeting (quick capture), Literature (notes from a source), Permanent (refined and standalone), Synthesis (cross-source consolidation).
inspector360.help_dim_review: Review — when this note was last intentionally reviewed. Shows the date or "Due" if the next review is past. Tracked by the Cognitive Engine's Review Pulse so old notes do not decay silently.
inspector360.help_dim_trails: Trails — the number of sequenced narratives this note participates in. Trails are paths through your library that you create in the Trails feature.
inspector360.help_dim_lenses: Lenses — the number of Multi-Lens groups this note belongs to. Lenses are thematic groupings (e.g. all notes tagged with a project or color).
inspector360.help_grand_total: Grand total — the count of every (deduped) connection to this note across all strata and link types. Equals the sum of the 8 column totals at the top, and equals the sum of the 8 row Σ totals on the right. If those three numbers diverge, the matrix derivation has a bug.
inspector360.help_hud_orphan: Orphan — this note has zero inbound links. Nothing in your library references it. Orphans are not always wrong, but they signal possible unintentional isolation.
inspector360.help_hud_fragile: Fragile — many notes link TO this one, but it has few derives-from links of its own. The note is load-bearing on a thin foundation. If you ever change or remove it, many dependents shake.
inspector360.help_hud_blind_spots: Blind spots — typed link directions you have not used for this note. With 7 typed directions available, having 5 blind spots means only 2 of the seven directions of reasoning have been declared for this note.
inspector360.help_hud_tensions: Tensions — active disagreements with this note (Contradicts links pointing at it). Tensions are not problems to fix; they are knowledge to develop. A note with multiple tensions is a note where your thinking is alive.

L.title: Link Types — wedge by typed-link kind

empty.provenance: Most of your universe is unsourced. Provenance mode reveals the shape of your epistemic content once notes are classified.

aristotelian.name: Aristotelian
aristotelian.tooltip: Aristotelian — Western-classical, knowledge as maturity gradient
aristotelian.scope: For any content; the default Sight grammar (stratum × time).

pramana.name: pramāṇa
pramana.tooltip: pramāṇa — Nyāya fourfold valid means of knowing
pramana.scope: For epistemological analysis of cognitive acts: perception, inference, analogy, testimony.

masadir.name: masādir
masadir.tooltip: masādir — Sunni uṣūl al-fiqh, sources as kinds of proof
masadir.scope: For Sunni Islamic legal-scholarly content. Not designed for secular or non-Islamic content.

polanyi.name: Polanyi
polanyi.tooltip: Polanyi — modern pluralism, tacit as the proximal pole
polanyi.scope: For knowledge with a tacit-vs-explicit dimension; what you know vs. what you can articulate.

mohist-san-biao.name: Mohist sān biǎo
mohist-san-biao.tooltip: Mohist sān biǎo — three standards as tests of doctrines
mohist-san-biao.scope: For doctrines tested by historical precedent / observational evidence / social benefit.

peirce.name: Peirce
peirce.tooltip: Peirce — American pragmatist, 3 phaneroscopic categories (Firstness / Secondness / Thirdness)
peirce.scope: For phenomenological classification: quality/feeling (Firstness), reaction/relation (Secondness), mediation/law (Thirdness).

habermas.name: Habermas
habermas.tooltip: Habermas — Frankfurt School critical theory, 3 knowledge-constitutive interests
habermas.scope: For knowledge classified by orientation: prediction/control (technical), mutual understanding (practical), reflection/liberation (emancipatory).

dewey.name: Dewey
dewey.tooltip: Dewey — pragmatist 5-stage pattern of inquiry (cyclic flow)
dewey.scope: For knowledge as the resolution of an indeterminate situation through inquiry: indeterminate → problem → hypothesis → reasoning → testing (and back).

husserl.name: Husserl
husserl.tooltip: Husserl — phenomenological regional ontologies (4 concentric zones)
husserl.scope: For knowledge classified by ontological region: formal ontology (center), material nature, animal nature, spirit / Geist (outer).

longino.name: Longino
longino.tooltip: Longino — Critical Contextual Empiricism, 4 norms of objective inquiry
longino.scope: For social conditions of objectivity: venues (public forums), uptake (response to criticism), public standards (shared criteria), tempered equality (credentialed disagreement).

ibn-rushd-burhan.name: Ibn Rushd burhān
ibn-rushd-burhan.tooltip: Ibn Rushd (Averroes) — 4 concentric demonstrative arts ranked by epistemic force
ibn-rushd-burhan.scope: For Islamic Aristotelian commentary tradition: burhān (apodictic demonstration, innermost), jadal (dialectic), khaṭāba (rhetoric), shiʿr (poetics, outermost).

shatibi-maqasid.name: Shāṭibī maqāṣid
shatibi-maqasid.tooltip: al-Shāṭibī — maqāṣid al-sharīʿa: 5 universal essentials × 3 tiers of necessity (15-cell grid)
shatibi-maqasid.scope: For Sunni Islamic legal-purpose analysis: each note at the intersection of an essential (dīn / nafs / ʿaql / nasl / māl) and a tier (ḍarūriyyāt / ḥājiyyāt / taḥsīniyyāt).

ibn-khaldun-umran.name: Ibn Khaldūn ʿumrān
ibn-khaldun-umran.tooltip: Ibn Khaldūn — ʿilm al-ʿumrān: bedouin↔urban cyclical civilizational dynamic
ibn-khaldun-umran.scope: For Islamic philosophical historiography: ḥaḍarī (sedentary/urban) above, badawī (nomadic/rural) below; cyclic arrows convey the bidirectional generational cycle of ʿaṣabiyya rise + decay.

pardes.name: PaRDeS
pardes.tooltip: PaRDeS — 4 levels of Torah interpretation, literal to mystical (Hebrew acronym)
pardes.scope: For Jewish hermeneutical analysis: peshat (literal, innermost) → remez (allusion) → derash (interpretive) → sod (mystical, outermost).

maimonidean-prophecy.name: Maimonidean prophecy
maimonidean-prophecy.tooltip: Maimonides — 11 degrees of prophecy in Guide of the Perplexed II:45 (spiral ladder)
maimonidean-prophecy.scope: For Jewish philosophical theology: 11 ascending degrees of prophetic experience, from ruaḥ ha-qodesh (holy spirit, innermost) to angel-vision-while-awake (Moses-level, outermost).

talmudic-middot.name: Talmudic 13 middot
talmudic-middot.tooltip: Rabbi Yishmael — 13 hermeneutical rules for interpreting Torah (Baraita d'Rabbi Yishmael, Sifra intro)
talmudic-middot.scope: For Talmudic hermeneutics: 13 logical rules ascending from simplest (kal va-chomer = a fortiori inference) to most complex (reconciliation of contradictory verses).

mencian-sprouts.name: Mencian sprouts
mencian-sprouts.tooltip: Mencius — 4 moral sprouts (端 duān) + optional central xìn (信 trustworthiness)
mencian-sprouts.scope: For Confucian moral psychology: 4 innate sprouts → 4 cardinal virtues (compassion → rén, shame → yì, deference → lǐ, right-wrong → zhì); central xìn binds them.

wang-yangming.name: Wang Yangming
wang-yangming.tooltip: Wang Yangming — zhī-xíng héyī: knowing and acting unified through innate moral knowing
wang-yangming.scope: For Neo-Confucian moral epistemology: zhī (knowing) ↔ liángzhī (innate moral knowing, center) ↔ xíng (acting). Bidirectional flow conveys the unity of knowledge and action.

korean-songnihak.name: Korean Sŏngnihak
korean-songnihak.tooltip: Yi T'oegye + Yi Yulgok — Four-Seven debate: lǐ vs qì × 四端 vs 七情 (16th-c. Korean Neo-Confucian)
korean-songnihak.scope: For Korean Neo-Confucian debate: 2×2 grid mapping the lǐ (principle) vs qì (psychophysical force) axis against the 四端 (4 sprouts) vs 七情 (7 emotions) axis.

mignolo-pluriversal.name: Mignolo pluriversal
mignolo-pluriversal.tooltip: Walter Mignolo — pluriversality: 5 decolonial positions around the modernity/totality hub
mignolo-pluriversal.scope: For Latin American decolonial analysis: central modernity/totality hub + 5 outer cluster bubbles (epistemic disobedience, border thinking, delinking, decolonial gnosis, pluriversal world).

dussel-transmodernity.name: Dussel transmodernity
dussel-transmodernity.tooltip: Enrique Dussel — totality (inner disc) ↔ exteriority (outer ring) with bidirectional analectic flow
dussel-transmodernity.scope: For liberation philosophy: concentric binary-flow with inner totality (modernity's encompassing system) and outer exteriority (what totality excludes — the colonized, the poor, the Other).

maldonado-torres.name: Maldonado-Torres
maldonado-torres.tooltip: Nelson Maldonado-Torres — three tiers of coloniality (power / knowledge / being)
maldonado-torres.scope: For decolonial analysis of persistent colonial structures: 3 concentric tiers — coloniality of power (political/economic, innermost), coloniality of knowledge (epistemic, middle), coloniality of being (ontological/existential, outermost).

akan-wiredu.name: Akan Wiredu
akan-wiredu.tooltip: Kwasi Wiredu — Akan epistemic vocabulary reconstructed for conceptual decolonization
akan-wiredu.scope: For African analytic philosophy: 3 Akan categories — nokware (truth / correspondence), ahonyam (well-being / reality-fittingness), adwene (mind / reflective thought).

ibuanyidanda.name: Ibuanyidanda
ibuanyidanda.tooltip: Innocent Asouzu — complementary ontology: every being constituted through its complementary relations to the missing link
ibuanyidanda.scope: For African philosophy of complementarity: central "missing link" hub + 5 entity-clusters (self / other / community / tradition / transcendence), each constitutively related to the unifying complementarity.

time-dome.name: Time Dome
time-dome.tooltip: Time Dome — when did you create your knowledge? Stars positioned by their creation month around the calendar rim.
time-dome.scope: For temporal analysis of your knowledge — which months produced the most notes, where are the gaps, how creation rhythm maps onto maturity strata.

canonical.adoptDesc: Files are renamed with structured IDs internally. Your titles stay human-readable everywhere. Best for users committed to Constellation.

canonical.keepDesc: Your files stay exactly as they are. Constellation adds a small identifier to each file's metadata — nothing else changes.
